title: A failing Python test command can be overwritten by the following passing command
observed_behavior: Each PowerShell block runs Python unittest discovery, then a second native unittest process, and checks $LASTEXITCODE only after the second process.
expected_invariant: Every required native test process must be checked independently so any nonzero result makes the job and aggregate gate fail.
root_cause: The workflow treats PowerShell's mutable process-global $LASTEXITCODE as an aggregate status instead of capturing or checking each native invocation immediately.
failure_scenario: tests/python returns exit 1 for a real regression, the non-browser WebView suite returns 0, the final conditional sees 0, and both the core job and the downstream complete-matrix aggregator report success.
evidence: Static evidence: deep-audit lines 101-108 and phase1-drift lines 160-167 contain two native Python calls followed by only one final $LASTEXITCODE check.
Static control-flow reproduction: with first_exit=1 and second_exit=0, the second process replaces $LASTEXITCODE with 0 before the only branch evaluates it.
The aggregator in deep-audit lines 188-203 and phase1-drift lines 247-262 checks only job result strings and cannot recover the overwritten first failure.
No shell option or checked-command helper in either block converts the intermediate native exit into a terminating PowerShell error.
existing_safeguards: The second unittest result is checked, job aggregation requires both named jobs to report success, and later release/package jobs execute additional checks.
safeguard_gap: None of those safeguards preserves the first native process exit code; later suites are overlapping but not a semantic substitute for every tests/python failure.
tests_present: Repository Python and non-browser WebView suites exist and are invoked.
Release self-test independently runs several unittest discovery groups.
tests_missing: Workflow regression that forces the first native command nonzero and the second zero and asserts the step fails.
A shared checked-native-command wrapper test covering every multi-command pwsh block.
recommended_remediation: After each Python process, capture the exit code and throw/exit immediately on nonzero, or invoke both through a checked helper that accumulates failures without overwriting them.
remediation_risk: low: control flow changes only failure propagation, though workflow tests should confirm diagnostic output from both suites remains useful.
validation_rung: Rung 6-equivalent CI validation: static workflow policy test plus hosted phase1/deep run with a temporary forced first-suite failure and passing second suite.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-workflow semantic defect. The 2026-07-19 audit recorded many direct unittest passes but did not prove this two-command workflow failure path.

title: Canonical test gates omit 26 pytest-style tests
observed_behavior: Both required CI workflows and the canonical release self-test use unittest discovery for tests/python; the workflows also assemble non-browser WebView unittest modules explicitly. None of these canonical gates runs pytest discovery.
expected_invariant: Every committed first-party test must be collected by at least one required CI or strict release gate with its runner declared in the dependency contract.
root_cause: The repository contains top-level pytest test functions while canonical CI and release-test discovery were built around unittest only, and pytest was never added to the declared development dependencies.
failure_scenario: A subtitle conversion, marketecture guard, dependency-atlas, or WebView touchpoint-ledger regression is caught only by one of the 26 pytest functions, but both required CI and a -RequireTests release self-test can stay green because none is collected.
evidence: Static inventory command rg -n '^def test_' tests/python tests/webview returned 28 matches; two are fixture strings in test_duplicate_test_name_report.py and the corrected executable count is 26.
The 26 tests are 7 in test_ass_to_srt_helpers.py, 11 in test_marketecture_guard.py, 2 in test_dependency_atlas.py, and 6 in test_webview_touchpoint_ledger.py.
Workflow lines use python -m unittest only.
Release test.ps1 lines 448-455 invokes Invoke-PythonUnittestDiscovery for desktop, core, and tooling; test_support.ps1 lines 238-256 hard-code unittest discover with no pytest branch.
requirements/dev.txt and pyproject.toml project dependencies do not declare pytest.
The W11 WebView-test completion run collected the pytest-only touchpoint tests and reproduced two live stale-ledger failures that unittest CI and the release self-test omit.
existing_safeguards: The tests are committed and can run under a locally provisioned pytest; private-beta runs pytest for three unrelated productization files.
safeguard_gap: There is no required workflow or release-self-test invocation, declared clean-environment runner, or collection reconciliation for these 26 tests.
tests_present: All 26 test bodies exist in four current files.
pyproject.toml defines pytest paths and Python path configuration.
tests_missing: CI and release-gate collection-count assertion covering the four files.
Clean dependency-install test proving pytest is available.
A guard that rejects top-level test functions outside canonical discovery.
recommended_remediation: Declare pytest in a test/development dependency set and add a required pytest invocation for the four files or all Python/WebView tests in both CI and the strict release self-test; alternatively convert the functions to unittest and enforce one framework.
remediation_risk: medium: enabling full pytest discovery may expose latent failures or duplicate execution and increases gate duration, so reconcile collection and ownership first.
validation_rung: Rung 1 plus Python/release test gating: clean install, pytest --collect-only count proof, execute all 26 tests in required CI, and run the strict release self-test with the same collection contract.
prior_audit_relationship: First identified by the current validation-spine inventory; prior unittest ledgers and release self-test passes are not evidence for top-level pytest functions.

title: The browser matrix selects only 23 of 34 modules and accepts unittest skips
observed_behavior: Each workflow hard-codes 29 method IDs from 23 browser modules and invokes raw unittest, while the current authoritative inventory contains 34 modules and the tests use unittest.SkipTest for missing browser prerequisites.
expected_invariant: A job described and aggregated as the browser matrix must derive from the complete current inventory and must treat zero tests or skips as missing evidence.
root_cause: The workflow duplicates a hand-maintained representative selector list and bypasses the shared strict browser runner that already enforces inventory/prerequisite outcomes.
failure_scenario: A regression exists only in one of 11 omitted modules, or Node/Chrome becomes unavailable and selected tests skip; the browser job still reports success and the aggregate labels the matrix complete.
evidence: Deterministic map comparison returned all_module_count=34, selected_module_count=23, omitted_module_count=11 for both workflows.
The omitted modules include evidence/lifecycle/pipeline-log/queue/root/run-monitor/safe-command/settings/control-census coverage, listed exactly in worker-10-ops-workflows.md.
Workflow invocations are raw python -m unittest at deep-audit line 186 and phase1-drift line 245.
Direct browser-test search found numerous unittest.SkipTest branches for missing Node or Chrome/Edge.
webview_browser_smoke_common.ps1 lines 199-219 and 262-271 fails zero tests and disallowed skips, proving the repository already has a strict path that CI does not use.
existing_safeguards: The selected matrix runs isolated with fail-fast false, required Node/media provisioning is attempted, and a strict wrapper plus generated 34-module map exists.
safeguard_gap: The selected IDs are not reconciled against the map and raw unittest does not apply the wrapper's skip/no-test policy.
tests_present: Strict wrapper support tests cover machine-readable prerequisite, skip, timeout, and zero-test outcomes.
Prior VAL-0035 executed all 34 current modules and 42 tests with zero skips as snapshot evidence.
tests_missing: Workflow/config test asserting every map module is selected exactly once.
Hosted workflow test proving missing Node/browser yields failure.
Drift guard that fails when a new browser module lacks matrix coverage.
recommended_remediation: Generate/shard the matrix from SMOKE_WRAPPER_MAP.json and call Invoke-WebViewBrowserSmokeUnittest without AllowSkippedTests; retain per-module structured results as artifacts.
remediation_risk: medium: complete strict execution increases Windows/browser minutes and may expose flaky or long modules, requiring bounded shards and timeouts.
validation_rung: Rung 1 strict browser validation across all 34 map-derived modules, followed by hosted phase1/deep workflow evidence with zero skips.
prior_audit_relationship: Prior VAL-0035 supplies compensating all-module proof for the 2026-07-20 snapshot, but it does not correct the current workflow selector/skip design.

title: Deep Audit and Audit SARIF push filters exclude ordinary code changes
observed_behavior: Both workflows list broad push branches but their paths arrays contain only their own workflow file.
expected_invariant: A push-triggered validation/security workflow must run when behavior, tests, dependencies, or scanner inputs it evaluates change, or be explicitly represented as scheduled-only evidence.
root_cause: The path filter was narrowed to workflow self-changes without enumerating the repositories surfaces consumed by the jobs.
failure_scenario: Code or dependency changes are pushed directly to a covered branch; neither Deep Audit nor Ruff/Semgrep SARIF runs, while observers infer branch-list coverage from the workflow configuration.
evidence: deep-audit lines 4-11 restrict push paths to .github/workflows/deep-audit.yml.
audit-sarif lines 4-11 restrict push paths to .github/workflows/audit-sarif.yml.
Deep Audit's weekly and Audit SARIF's daily schedules eventually run, but they are not commit-adjacent push evidence.
phase1-drift covers pull requests and main/master pushes, but not every named deep-audit feature branch push and not the Semgrep lane.
existing_safeguards: Both workflows have schedule and manual triggers; phase1-drift runs on all pull requests and main/master pushes; CodeQL runs on pull requests.
safeguard_gap: Those lanes are not equivalent to fresh Deep Audit/Semgrep evidence for the exact pushed commit, and direct feature-branch pushes can remain unscanned until schedule.
tests_present: check-github-audit-spine.ps1 verifies required workflow tokens are present.
tests_missing: Trigger-policy test against a representative path matrix.
Repository policy asserting which workflows must run for source/test/dependency/workflow changes.
recommended_remediation: Remove the self-only path filters or replace them with comprehensive source/test/config/dependency paths, and document any intentionally scheduled-only scanners.
remediation_risk: medium: broader triggers substantially increase CI usage, so use concurrency cancellation and path-grouped jobs rather than silently narrowing evidence.
validation_rung: Rung 6-equivalent workflow validation: trigger tests plus temporary source/test/dependency commits proving the intended hosted jobs enqueue.
prior_audit_relationship: Confirmed by the current validation-spine inventory; no prior disposition showed the self-only filters were intentional acceptance.

title: Named audit suites leave four available freshness checks outside their suite membership
observed_behavior: The current 19-check deep-audit suite and 13-check phase1-generated suite omit smoke-wrapper-map, duplicate-test-name-report, WebView inventory-doc checks, and context-slice checks.
expected_invariant: Named repository-wide audit orchestration should either run every maintained freshness check in its scope or explicitly document and compensate exclusions.
root_cause: Check registration and suite membership are maintained separately and no suite-coverage policy asserts inclusion or an intentional exclusion reason.
failure_scenario: A generated smoke map, duplicate-name report, WebView inventory document, or navigation capsule drifts while the named generated/deep suite remains green.
evidence: Current audit_checks.py lines 253-273 define 19 deep-audit members and include run-monitor-schema and legacy-reliability-inventory.
Current source confirms the four omitted checks; the earlier 17-check/run-monitor omission and 18-check count were corrected and are not used.
Release self-test later covers smoke-wrapper-map and duplicate-test-name-report, but no reviewed workflow job invokes generate_webview_inventory_docs --check or context_slice --check.
Root package webview:prework:check does not include either Python check.
existing_safeguards: Release self-test covers two omitted generators, WebView prework covers several JavaScript-generated surfaces, and each omitted tool has a direct check mode.
safeguard_gap: Two checks remain absent workflow-wide and the compensation for the other two is indirect and not expressed in suite membership.
tests_present: Individual generator/tool tests exist for smoke-map and related tooling.
release-self-test suite includes smoke-wrapper-map and duplicate-test-name-report.
tests_missing: Suite-membership policy test for all registered checks.
Hosted workflow assertion for WebView inventory-doc and context-slice freshness.
Explicit allowlist/reason mechanism for intentionally excluded checks.
recommended_remediation: Add the four checks to a suitable required suite/job, deduplicate the two later release checks, and add a manifest test requiring every registered freshness check to be included or intentionally exempted.
remediation_risk: low: checks are read-only, though duplicate execution and source-tree-only behavior in packaged contexts must be avoided.
validation_rung: Generated-context verification plus Rung 6 workflow run of the revised suite on clean and intentionally stale fixtures.
prior_audit_relationship: Current independent reconciliation is authoritative: 19 deep-audit checks with run-monitor-schema and legacy-reliability-inventory present; this finding records only the four actual exclusions.

title: PowerShell analysis uses an unpinned module and a helper that succeeds when the analyzer is absent
observed_behavior: Both workflows install PSScriptAnalyzer with Install-Module -Force and no version, then call a script that warns and exits 0 if no module is discoverable.
expected_invariant: Required static analysis must use a reproducible analyzer/rules version and fail closed when the analyzer cannot run.
root_cause: The workflows install whichever gallery version resolves at runtime, while the checker explicitly treats an undiscoverable analyzer as a successful skip.
failure_scenario: A gallery/module-discovery failure or runner drift leaves PSScriptAnalyzer unavailable; the helper warns and exits 0, so PowerShell violations are unexamined while the CI job stays green. A newly resolved module version can also change rules without a repository diff.
evidence: deep-audit lines 50-52 and phase1-drift lines 77-79 run Install-Module PSScriptAnalyzer -Force without RequiredVersion or a lock.
deep-audit lines 54-56 and phase1-drift lines 81-83 call ops/scripts/dev/check_powershell_analysis.ps1.
check_powershell_analysis.ps1 lines 21-24 emits a warning and exits 0 when Get-Module cannot find PSScriptAnalyzer.
The helper does fail when the target path is missing and when Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer returns findings, so the gap is specifically analyzer availability and version reproducibility.
existing_safeguards: The install step is explicit, the helper fails for a missing target path and reported analyzer findings, and both workflows expose logs.
safeguard_gap: No repository-pinned module version or checksum exists, and the helper converts the missing-analyzer prerequisite failure into success.
tests_present: Both Windows workflows invoke the checker against the engine path.
No dedicated repository test of the helper's missing-module branch was found.
tests_missing: A helper test asserting analyzer absence is fatal in CI.
A workflow/static assertion that PSScriptAnalyzer is version-pinned.
A canary proving the pinned ruleset runs on the supported Windows runner.
recommended_remediation: Pin an approved PSScriptAnalyzer version in repository-controlled dependency metadata, install that exact version, and make analyzer absence fatal for CI while retaining an explicitly opt-in local advisory mode if needed.
remediation_risk: low to medium: pinning is straightforward, but the chosen ruleset must be baselined before fail-closed enforcement.
validation_rung: Rung 6 release-validation canary on windows-latest plus a focused helper test that simulates an unavailable analyzer; no real media required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current semantic finding; prior green analysis evidence did not prove a pinned analyzer or fail-closed missing-module behavior.

title: Scanner failures and findings can leave Audit SARIF green, including when no SARIF exists
observed_behavior: Ruff and Semgrep execution are continue-on-error, and every summary/artifact/code-scanning step is conditional on the corresponding SARIF file existing.
expected_invariant: A green security-scan job must distinguish an accepted findings result from an operational scanner failure and must fail when required evidence is absent.
root_cause: The workflow uses blanket continue-on-error for scanner commands and file-existence guards for all downstream evidence without a final status/threshold adjudication step.
failure_scenario: Ruff or Semgrep crashes before writing SARIF, or Ruff returns nonzero for findings; downstream evidence steps skip or merely summarize, and the job completes successfully with no machine-enforced indication of failure or accepted findings.
evidence: audit-sarif lines 39-41 and 89-91 set continue-on-error: true on both scanner invocations.
Ruff summary/artifact/upload steps at lines 43-70 and Semgrep counterparts at lines 93-120 run only when hashFiles finds SARIF.
No unconditional step verifies that each scanner produced valid SARIF or classifies the scanner exit code.
The summaries count results but no later step compares counts with an approved baseline or threshold.
existing_safeguards: Jobs have timeouts, actions are commit-pinned, and artifact upload uses if-no-files-found: error when the upload step actually runs.
safeguard_gap: The file-existence condition prevents the artifact safeguard from running on the exact no-output failure it should expose, and findings/operational failures are not adjudicated separately.
tests_present: No dedicated repository test of scanner exit/no-SARIF behavior was found; scheduled and manual workflow runs provide observational evidence only.
tests_missing: Injected scanner crash proving no-SARIF fails the job.
Findings-producing fixture proving the configured acceptance policy.
Malformed SARIF validation and upload-failure handling test.
recommended_remediation: Capture each scanner exit code, require parseable SARIF unconditionally, distinguish findings exits from operational failures, and add a final policy step that fails on missing evidence or findings outside an approved baseline.
remediation_risk: medium: tightening the gate may initially surface accepted debt and requires an explicit baseline policy.
validation_rung: Rung 6 CI/release-evidence validation with controlled clean, findings, crash, and malformed-SARIF runs in a test branch or repository; no real media required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current semantic finding; prior artifact-presence checks did not cover the conditional no-output path or findings acceptance.

title: Ruff, Semgrep, and the Semgrep ruleset can drift without a repository change
observed_behavior: The workflow installs broad Ruff and Semgrep version ranges and invokes Semgrep's mutable remote p/default configuration.
expected_invariant: Audit evidence for a fixed commit should be reproducible from repository-pinned scanner binaries and rules.
root_cause: Scanner dependency constraints and Semgrep rule selection are resolved from moving external sources at run time rather than locked in repository-controlled inputs.
failure_scenario: Two scheduled runs of the same commit resolve different scanner versions or p/default rules and produce different findings, parsing behavior, or failures, making audit deltas impossible to attribute to code.
evidence: audit-sarif lines 36-37 install ruff>=0.8,<1 rather than an exact reviewed version.
audit-sarif lines 86-87 install semgrep>=1,<2 rather than an exact reviewed version.
audit-sarif lines 89-91 request the remote p/default ruleset with no committed config or digest.
The workflow emits finding counts but does not record resolved package/ruleset identities as evidence.
existing_safeguards: Major-version upper bounds reduce breaking-version exposure, and the workflow retains SARIF artifacts when generated.
safeguard_gap: Broad ranges and a moving remote ruleset still allow behavior changes inside the accepted ranges, while artifacts do not identify the ruleset digest.
tests_present: No repository test asserts exact scanner/ruleset identity; repeated scheduled runs provide only post hoc comparison.
tests_missing: Dependency-lock assertion for Ruff and Semgrep.
Committed Semgrep-config integrity test.
Evidence assertion recording scanner versions and ruleset digest.
recommended_remediation: Pin exact scanner versions, commit or digest-pin the Semgrep configuration, and record those identities in the job summary/SARIF provenance.
remediation_risk: low to medium: deterministic inputs are low risk, but ruleset pinning requires a deliberate update cadence.
validation_rung: Rung 6 audit-evidence validation: run the pinned lane twice at one commit and compare tool identities plus normalized SARIF; no real media required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current reproducibility finding; prior action SHA pinning did not extend to scanner packages or remote rules.

title: CodeQL is artifact-only by default and has no findings acceptance gate
observed_behavior: CodeQL analysis defaults upload to never, then only summarizes local result counts and uploads ordinary workflow artifacts without failing on findings.
expected_invariant: The repository's primary CodeQL lane should expose results to the intended code-scanning/branch-protection surface or enforce a documented artifact-only findings policy.
root_cause: Upload behavior is delegated to an optional repository variable with a non-uploading default, and no baseline/threshold adjudication exists for the local SARIF path.
failure_scenario: CodeQL succeeds while reporting serious findings; the check remains green, no code-scanning alerts/status are created by default, and reviewers must manually download four language artifacts to discover the results.
evidence: codeql lines 47-53 set analyze.upload to vars.CODEQL_UPLOAD_MODE || 'never'.
codeql lines 55-76 only count SARIF results and print them to the step summary.
codeql lines 78-84 upload SARIF as a generic artifact.
No subsequent step fails on finding count or accepted-baseline drift.
existing_safeguards: Operational CodeQL failures are not ignored, queries include security-extended and security-and-quality, actions are commit-pinned, and SARIF artifacts are retained.
safeguard_gap: Successful analysis is not equivalent to accepted findings, and the default prevents the platform's alert/status surface from receiving results.
tests_present: No dedicated repository test of CODEQL_UPLOAD_MODE/default behavior or findings gating was found.
tests_missing: Workflow-policy assertion for the intended upload default.
Known-finding fixture proving alert/threshold behavior.
Branch-protection integration check for CodeQL result visibility.
recommended_remediation: Default to the repository's approved code-scanning upload mode and enforce an explicit alert/baseline policy; if artifact-only operation is intentional, rename and document the lane as non-gating evidence with automated result adjudication.
remediation_risk: medium: enabling uploads or gating may surface existing alerts and requires triage/baseline ownership.
validation_rung: Rung 6 CI/release-evidence validation with a known-finding branch, verifying upload/alert visibility and the documented acceptance policy; no real media required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current semantic finding; prior CodeQL action pinning and artifact retention did not establish findings visibility or acceptance.

title: The private-beta workflow does not provision pytest by contract on a clean runner
observed_behavior: The workflow copies setup-python into the bundled runtime without installing project/test dependencies, then invokes that copied runtime with -m pytest even though pytest is undeclared.
expected_invariant: Every executable/import used by a clean release runner must be declared and provisioned deterministically before a signed build can proceed.
root_cause: The release workflow assumes incidental contents of the setup-python toolcache/local bundled runtime instead of using the initializer's dependency-install mode and declaring pytest.
failure_scenario: A clean or updated Windows runner supplies Python and pip but not pytest; the productization test step exits with No module named pytest and the signed-installer lane cannot proceed.
evidence: private-beta line 96 invokes Initialize-CiPythonRuntime.ps1 without -InstallDependencies.
Initializer lines 126-133 install requirements only when that switch is present.
apps/desktop/runtime and ops/pipeline/runtime are gitignored, so clean checkout does not provide the locally observed pytest installation.
Workflow lines 133-137 invoke apps/desktop/runtime/Python/python.exe -m pytest.
requirements/dev.txt and pyproject.toml dependencies omit pytest; git ls-files found no tracked pytest package under the runtime.
The pytest step is not continue-on-error and occurs before signing/build publication steps, so the missing module stops the job before any release mutation.
existing_safeguards: actions/setup-python installs Python 3.11; the initializer validates copied Python; the local developer runtime currently contains pytest 9.1.0.
safeguard_gap: Neither hosted-toolcache packages nor ignored local runtime contents are reproducible release dependencies.
tests_present: Three productization pytest files are explicitly selected.
Other CI workflows call Initialize-CiPythonRuntime.ps1 -InstallDependencies.
tests_missing: Clean Windows runner provisioning test.
Dependency contract assertion that every invoked Python module is declared.
Private-beta workflow dry-run using an empty runtime target.
recommended_remediation: Declare pytest in a reviewed test dependency set, call the initializer with dependency installation, and validate import pytest plus project imports before running tests.
remediation_risk: low: provisioning becomes explicit, with only additional install time and version-selection work.
validation_rung: Rung 6 private-beta workflow run from a clean Windows runner/cache, proving dependency installation and all three pytest files execute.
prior_audit_relationship: Independent review confirms the root and calibrates the direct impact to P2: prior local bundled-runtime success does not close clean-runner reproducibility, but the missing dependency fails closed before signing or publication.

title: The configured beta updater endpoint cannot resolve the beta prerelease
observed_behavior: Beta publication creates a prerelease, while the generated updater endpoint uses GitHub's releases/latest alias for latest-beta.json.
expected_invariant: A beta client's configured endpoint must resolve the channel metadata asset published by the most recent approved beta release.
root_cause: The productization config uses a single full-release latest alias for both stable and beta channels rather than a channel-specific pointer.
failure_scenario: A beta installer checks for updates; GitHub's latest alias resolves only a non-prerelease full release, so latest-beta.json is absent/stale and beta update discovery returns 404 or the wrong channel metadata.
evidence: private-beta lines 216-218 add --prerelease for every non-stable channel.
New-TauriProductizationConfig.ps1 line 47 generates https://github.com/<repo>/releases/latest/download/latest-<channel>.json for beta and stable.
Test-PrivateBetaReleasePreflight.ps1 lines 147-148 asserts the same beta latest URL rather than exercising it.
GitHub official Releases documentation defines latest as the most recent non-prerelease, non-draft full release and says prereleases cannot be latest.
The workflow uploads latest-beta.json to the versioned prerelease tag, not to a separate stable channel location.
existing_safeguards: Channel JSON contains a versioned installer URL/signature and local artifact verification checks its contents; published-release tooling checks beta is marked prerelease.
safeguard_gap: No test requests the exact configured endpoint after publication, and local consistency cannot prove GitHub alias resolution.
tests_present: test_private_beta_release_preflight.py asserts the generated URL.
Private-beta artifact/published-release tests verify by-tag assets and prerelease state.
tests_missing: Post-publish HTTP check of the exact beta endpoint.
Updater client integration against a real prerelease.
Stable/beta channel-pointer behavior test.
recommended_remediation: Publish beta channel metadata at a stable channel-specific URL or maintain an explicit channel pointer outside GitHub's full-release latest alias, then make post-publish endpoint retrieval a gate.
remediation_risk: medium to high: updater endpoint changes affect installed clients and require a compatible migration/rollback plan.
validation_rung: Rung 6 release validation in an isolated test repository: publish prerelease, retrieve exact configured endpoint, verify signature/version, and perform updater canary; no real media required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current semantic finding; prior private-beta tests encoded the endpoint string but did not validate GitHub prerelease resolution.

title: The private-beta workflow can publish without the repository's strict release acceptance
observed_behavior: The beta/stable publish lane runs three pytest files, cargo check, and artifact signature/layout checks but never invokes test.ps1 -RequireTests or deployable/package runtime verification.
expected_invariant: The exact commit being signed and published must pass the canonical strict release, Tauri/Rust, package, and operator-surface acceptance gates.
root_cause: Productization artifact validation was treated as release acceptance, while the strict validation spine remains in separate workflows with no required status/commit binding.
failure_scenario: An operator dispatches publish_release for a commit with a core, browser, PowerShell, Rust-test, tool-integration, E2E, or package-runtime regression; the installer is validly signed and uploaded because metadata checks pass.
evidence: private-beta lines 130-137 run only three productization pytest files.
Line 142 runs npm run check; apps/desktop/tauri/package.json maps check only to cargo check, not cargo test.
build.ps1 -DryRun -Zip at line 128 copies nothing and explicitly skips verification in dry-run mode.
The workflow never references ops/scripts/release/test.ps1 -RequireTests, although deep-audit and phase1-drift do.
Test-PrivateBetaReleaseArtifact verifies installer/signature/channel JSON/checksums/Authenticode, not application behavior.
affected_flows: beta and stable signed installer publication
existing_safeguards: Input preflight, three productization tests, cargo check, signed NSIS build, Authenticode validation, updater signature and checksum checks, and optional protected environments.
safeguard_gap: Artifact integrity proves what was built, not that the product passed the repository's release-critical behavior gates at that SHA.
tests_present: Productization contract tests and local artifact verifier.
Canonical test.ps1 -RequireTests and package verification exist in other workflows.
tests_missing: Required status/SHA binding to strict release workflow.
Rust cargo test in publish lane.
Package open/close and ToolIntegration/E2E evidence for the signed artifact.
Negative dispatch test refusing unvalidated commit.
recommended_remediation: Run or require successful strict release self-test, Rust tests, and package/runtime verification for the exact GITHUB_SHA before exposing signing secrets or enabling publication.
remediation_risk: medium: release duration and runner requirements increase, and status binding across workflows must avoid trusting stale/different commits.
validation_rung: Rung 6 complete release/package validation for the exact signed SHA, followed by isolated private-beta publish and installed-layout/open-close verification.
prior_audit_relationship: New cross-workflow release finding; prior direct validation evidence exists but the reviewed publish workflow does not require or bind it.

title: Version, tag, commit, and existing-release identity are not bound before asset clobber
observed_behavior: Version and release tag are independently format-validated; an existing release is accepted after gh release view and current assets are uploaded with --clobber without verifying the release's target commit or channel identity.
expected_invariant: A release tag, semantic version, source commit, channel/prerelease state, and asset set must form one immutable provenance identity; replacement must require an explicit protected rebuild policy.
root_cause: Validation checks syntactic shape and local self-consistency but never establishes identity equality or immutability against existing remote release state.
failure_scenario: Inputs use version B with tag app-vA, or reuse app-vA from a different commit; the workflow builds B/current HEAD, generates metadata using the supplied pair, and replaces assets under A's existing release/tag.
evidence: Workflow lines 65-69 validate version and tag with independent regular expressions.
Test-PrivateBetaReleasePreflight.ps1 lines 58-61 repeats independent format checks and never asserts ReleaseTag equals app-v plus Version.
Existing release path lines 200-220 checks only gh release view success; no target_commitish/tag SHA/title/channel/prerelease comparison occurs.
Lines 221-226 use gh release upload --clobber.
Local artifact verification compares metadata to the same independent inputs and cannot detect mismatch with the remote tag commit.
existing_safeguards: Inputs have constrained character/length shapes; new releases target GITHUB_SHA; generated channel JSON is internally checked; environment approvals may restrict operators.
safeguard_gap: Valid format is not semantic identity, and existing releases bypass the only --target GITHUB_SHA creation argument.
tests_present: Private-beta preflight/artifact/published-release tests cover format, by-tag URLs, titles, prerelease flag, signature, and checksum presence.
tests_missing: Mismatched version/tag negative test.
Existing tag pointing at a different SHA negative test.
Wrong channel/prerelease/title existing-release test.
Protected explicit same-SHA rebuild test.
recommended_remediation: Require ReleaseTag == app-v<Version>, resolve and compare tag/release target to GITHUB_SHA, verify channel/title state, make versioned assets immutable by default, and require a separately protected same-SHA rebuild override before replacement.
remediation_risk: medium to high: tightening identity can disrupt current rebuild practices and requires a documented revocation/reissue path rather than silent clobber.
validation_rung: Rung 6 release tests in an isolated repository for matching new release, mismatched inputs, same-tag different SHA, same-SHA protected rebuild, and immutable asset behavior.
prior_audit_relationship: New current release-provenance finding; no prior audit disposition demonstrated remote tag/commit identity enforcement.

title: Release signing credentials are exposed to every job step
observed_behavior: Updater private key/password and Windows certificate material/password are declared at job scope, making them available to setup actions, dependency lifecycle scripts, repository tests, and all other processes.
expected_invariant: High-value signing credentials must be exposed only to the minimum reviewed signing/import step after untrusted dependency and test execution completes.
root_cause: Convenient job-level environment configuration replaced per-step secret scoping and separation of unprivileged validation from protected signing.
failure_scenario: A compromised npm dependency lifecycle script, third-party action, or repository test executed before signing reads the job environment and exfiltrates the updater key or certificate credentials.
evidence: private-beta lines 37-46 define all signing/certificate values under jobs.build-windows.env.
The scope therefore covers checkout/setup actions, preflight, npm ci, dry-run packaging, pytest, and cargo check before the signing build.
Only certificate import needs WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_BASE64/PASSWORD and only the Tauri signing build needs TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY/PASSWORD.
Actions are pinned and environment secrets are masked, but masking does not prevent a process from reading or transmitting values.
existing_safeguards: Secrets come from named GitHub environments, are masked in logs, actions are commit-pinned, and the runner is ephemeral.
safeguard_gap: Environment approval controls when the whole job starts, not which steps can read secrets; pinned dependencies/repository code still execute with unnecessary credential access.
tests_present: Preflight verifies required secret presence without intentionally printing values.
tests_missing: Sentinel-secret scope test proving install/test steps cannot read signing values.
Workflow policy test rejecting job-level signing secrets.
Separated unprivileged-validation/protected-signing integration test.
recommended_remediation: Split validation and signing into separate jobs, pass only nonsecret verified artifacts across the boundary, and scope each signing/certificate secret to the exact import or build step that consumes it.
remediation_risk: medium to high: Tauri signing environment requirements and cross-job artifact integrity must be preserved without writing secrets into artifacts or logs.
validation_rung: Rung 6 isolated release workflow with sentinel credentials, proving pre-signing steps lack access while signed artifacts and verification still succeed.
prior_audit_relationship: New current secret-boundary finding; prior checks confirmed secret presence and environment binding but did not review step-level exposure.

title: Concurrent private-release dispatches can race creation and clobber assets
observed_behavior: The workflow has no concurrency group, while publication performs a non-atomic release view, conditional create, and clobbering upload.
expected_invariant: Only one publication transaction per repository/channel/tag may mutate release state at a time, and channel advancement must be atomic or recoverable.
root_cause: Manual environment approval is treated as serialization, but GitHub Actions permits overlapping approved dispatches and the publish logic has no lock/idempotency token.
failure_scenario: Two operators or retries dispatch the same channel/tag; both build independently, race release creation, and then replace installer/signature/channel/checksum assets in last-writer-wins order, potentially mixing evidence and artifacts.
evidence: No top-level or job-level concurrency key exists in private-beta-windows.yml lines 1-226.
Publication lines 200-220 separates gh release view from conditional create.
Lines 221-226 uploads multiple assets with --clobber.
The environment name is channel-scoped, but GitHub environments do not inherently serialize jobs unless deployment/concurrency settings explicitly do so outside source.
existing_safeguards: Manual dispatch, optional environment approvals, local artifact consistency checks, and per-command GitHub API conflict behavior reduce accidental execution.
safeguard_gap: No source-controlled serialization or remote-state transaction binds the locally verified artifact set to the final uploaded set.
tests_present: Single-run private-beta dry-run/readiness/artifact tests.
tests_missing: Two-run same-channel/tag concurrency test.
Interrupted/partial upload recovery test.
Idempotent retry and asset-set atomicity test.
recommended_remediation: Add a repository/channel concurrency group with cancel-in-progress false, reject duplicate in-progress tags, publish immutable versioned assets first, and advance a channel pointer only after the full set verifies.
remediation_risk: medium: serialization affects release throughput and channel-pointer design must preserve safe retries after partial failures.
validation_rung: Rung 6 isolated GitHub test-repository exercise with two simultaneous dispatches, forced interruption, retry, and final asset/signature/checksum coherence assertions.
prior_audit_relationship: New current release-concurrency finding; prior generic concurrency review did not cover this publication transaction.
